q_en: Why does the last letter of a word keep changing?
not_yet: The names of all the cases and every rule for them: this lesson gives the three jobs only.
Dual and sound plural endings in full: you meet them as words.
Words whose ending never changes: later.
not_yet_ar: أَسْمَاءُ الْحَالَاتِ كُلِّهَا وَكُلُّ قَوَاعِدِهَا: الْيَوْمَ نَتَعَلَّمُ الْأَعْمَالَ الثَّلَاثَةَ فَقَطْ.
الْمُثَنَّى وَجَمْعُ الْمُذَكَّرِ السَّالِمُ بِالتَّفْصِيلِ: تَلْقَاهُمَا كَلِمَاتٍ.
كَلِمَاتٌ لَا تَتَغَيَّرُ نِهَايَتُهَا: فِي دَرْسٍ لَاحِقٍ.

lines: Which letters of الطَّالِب stay? Which one changes?
Who is doing? Whom did I hear? What follows إِلَى?
مَنْ يَفْعَلُ؟ وَمَنْ سَمِعْتُ؟ وَمَاذَا بَعْدَ «إِلَى»؟
Would a different ending change the meaning?
هَلْ يَتَغَيَّرُ الْمَعْنَى إِذَا تَغَيَّرَتِ النِّهَايَةُ؟

cards.def_en: the doer, or what the sentence is about (with tanwin: ـٌ)
what the action reaches, or the statement after كَانَ (with tanwin: ـًا)
after إِلَى مِنْ فِي …, and the second word of an “of” phrase (with tanwin: ـٍ)

slides.note: The sound plural of people has two forms; a broken plural changes like a single word.
slides.note_ar: لِلْجَمْعِ السَّالِمِ شَكْلَانِ، وَجَمْعُ التَّكْسِيرِ يَتَغَيَّرُ كَالْمُفْرَدِ.

slides.head_en: Some words refuse tanwin and kasra
slides.head_ar: كَلِمَاتٌ لَا تَقْبَلُ التَّنْوِينَ وَلَا الْكَسْرَةَ

cards.title_en: A word that refuses tanwin (a diptote)
cards.def_en: No tanwin. Where ـِ is expected, it takes ـَ.
an alif after the second letter, then two more letters

slides.head_en: An ordinary word, or one that refuses?
slides.tip: It has ـُ when doing and ـَ in the other two jobs. It never shows ـِ.
slides.tip_ar: ـُ لِلرَّفْعِ، وَـَ لِلنَّصْبِ وَالْجَرِّ. لَا كَسْرَةَ وَلَا تَنْوِينَ.

slides.head_en: Five nouns write their ending as a long vowel
slides.note: The long vowel shows only before a word or ending. Alone they are ordinary: أَبٌ, أَخٌ.
slides.note_ar: تَظْهَرُ الْحُرُوفُ إِذَا جَاءَ بَعْدَهَا كَلِمَةٌ. وَحْدَهَا: أَبٌ، أَخٌ.

slides.head_en: Try: read the ending, say the job
items: أَبُو: ـُ, so he is doing: Ahmad’s father went
after مَعَ: ـِ (ي): with his brother
ـَ (ا): the one I heard: your brother
a name that refuses: ـَ after إِلَى: to Tarim
ذُو: ـُ like رَجُلٌ: a man of knowledge
a long plural that refuses: ـَ after فِي: in mosques
the statement after كَانَ ends in ـًا: his father was generous
“of”: أَبِي ـِ, and عُمَرَ refuses: ـَ: ʿUmar’s father’s book

slides.why: A student writes تَرِيمٍ with tanwin and kasra. Wrong! Tarīm refuses both: إِلَى تَرِيمَ.
slides.why_ar: كَتَبَ طَالِبٌ «تَرِيمٍ» بِالتَّنْوِينِ وَالْكَسْرَةِ. هَذَا خَطَأٌ! تَرِيمُ لَا تَقْبَلُهُمَا: إِلَى تَرِيمَ.

lines: ذَهَبَ أَحْمَدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ سَالِمٍ إِلَى تَرِيمَ مَعَ أَبِي عُمَرَ.

وَجَلَسَ مَعَ أَخِي فَاطِمَةَ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ.
And he sat with Fatima’s brother in the mosque.

can_ar: أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَقْرَأَ النِّهَايَاتِ الثَّلَاثَ (ـُ ـَ ـِ) وَأَقُولَ عَمَلَ كُلٍّ مِنْهَا.

sections.name: A
sections.en: Read the story: to Tarim with his father. Then answer.
lines: ذَهَبَ أَحْمَدُ مَعَ أَبِيهِ إِلَى تَرِيمَ.
Ahmad went with his father to Tarim.
دَخَلَ أَحْمَدُ الْمَسْجِدَ الْكَبِيرَ وَجَلَسَ مَعَ عُمَرَ.
Ahmad entered the big mosque and sat with ʿUmar.
وَسَأَلَ أَبُو أَحْمَدَ عَنْ أَخِيهِ، وَهُوَ رَجُلٌ ذُو عِلْمٍ.
And Ahmad’s father asked about his brother, who is a man of knowledge.
The Habib said: Your brother is in the ribāṭ.
فَذَهَبَ أَبُو أَحْمَدَ إِلَى الرِّبَاطِ وَرَأَى أَخَاهُ.
So Ahmad’s father went to the ribāṭ and saw his brother.
قَالَ أَخُو أَبِيهِ لِأَحْمَدَ: هَلْ أَنْتَ طَالِبُ عِلْمٍ؟
His father’s brother said to Ahmad: Are you a student of knowledge?
قَالَ أَحْمَدُ: نَعَمْ، أَنَا طَالِبُ عِلْمٍ.
Ahmad said: Yes, I am a student of knowledge.

sections.name: W
sections.en: The Story Strip: lines 1–69
lines: A boy went to a mosque.
The boy sat in the mosque.
The boy opened a muṣḥaf (a copy of the Qur’an).
The boy read in the muṣḥaf.
The boy sat in the study circle.
The friends went to the mosque.
The students read in the books.
The Habib sat in the mosque.
The Habib is a righteous man.
Is the Habib in the mosque?
Yes, the Habib is in the mosque.
The boy came in through the door.
The mother looked at the boy.
The boy sits in the study circle today.
Maryam is reading the muṣḥaf now.
The boy was happy in the majlis.
Maryam was happy in the study circle.
The boy did not leave the majlis.
لَنْ يَجْلِسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْبَيْتِ غَدًا.
The boy will not sit at home tomorrow.
ذَهَبَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْأَبِ إِلَى الزِّيَارَةِ.
The boy went with the father to the ziyāra (the visit).
The boy sat with good manners in the majlis.
The boy heard the Rātib (the litany) with his father.
ذَهَبَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الصَّبَاحِ إِلَى بَيْتِ الْحَبِيبِ.
The boy went in the morning to the Habib’s house.
The boy sat in the circle of dhikr (remembrance of Allah).
The Habib asked him about the lesson.
The boy served the guests and carried the food.
ثُمَّ جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْحَبِيبِ وَسَمِعَ الدَّرْسَ.
Then the boy sat with the Habib and heard the lesson.
The guests thanked the boy who served them.
حَفِظَ الْوَلَدُ مَا سَمِعَ مِنَ الْحَبِيبِ.
The boy memorised what he heard from the Habib.
فَهِمَ الْوَلَدُ الدَّرْسَ لِأَنَّهُ خَدَمَ الضُّيُوفَ.
The boy understood the lesson because he served the guests.
فِي الْمَجْلِسِ خَمْسَةُ ضُيُوفٍ وَسَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ كُلَّ كَلِمَةٍ.
There are five guests in the majlis, and the boy heard every word.
جَاءَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الرِّبَاطِ فِي الصَّبَاحِ.
The boy came to the ribāṭ in the morning.
The Habib said: Knowledge is light.
سَأَلَ عُمَرُ صَدِيقَهُ: هَلْ أَنْتَ ذَاهِبٌ إِلَى الرَّوْحَةِ؟
Umar asked his friend: Are you going to the rawḥa?
سَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ مِنَ الْحَبِيبِ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: الصَّلَاةُ نُورٌ.
The boy heard from the Habib: The Prophet ﷺ said: Prayer is light.
The boy opened his muṣḥaf and read his wird (his daily portion).
صَلَّى الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الطُّلَّابِ ثُمَّ دَعَا.
The boy prayed with the students, then made duʿāʾ.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ الْمَوْلِدَ لِأَنَّ مَحَبَّةَ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ فِي قَلْبِهِ.
The boy read the mawlid because love of the Prophet ﷺ is in his heart.
قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ لِأَبِي الْوَلَدِ: وَلَدُكَ طَالِبُ عِلْمٍ.
The Habib said to the boy’s father: Your son is a student of knowledge (ṭālib ʿilm).

items.en: Translate the two new lines into English.
items.model: The Habib said to the boy’s father: Your son is a student of knowledge. The boy’s father praised Allah.

items.en: In the first new line, which form of “father” follows لِ, and what is its ending?
items.model: أَبِي (the ending ـِ after a preposition)
items.note: the ending ـِ after a preposition

items.en: In the second new line, which form of “father” is the one doing it, and what is its ending?
items.model: أَبُو (the ending ـُ for the one doing it)
items.note: the ending ـُ for the one doing it

items.en: Write in Arabic: The boy’s father praised Allah.
